The '''Church of Infinite Perception''' was a rigid, fundamentalist religious organization of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Pergitor]]. The [[The Preceptor|leaders]] of the Church had been exiled<ref name="HNN 46>''{{HoloNetNewsWeb|46|regional/1337_4.html|Pergitor Coup Leaves Thousands Dead}}''</ref> during the 15-year timespan where Pergitor's government had become liberal, but they still managed to gain many followers by taking advantage of the dissatisfied sentiment shared by many conservatives on the world.<ref name="GG6.2" /> Launching a [[Coup on Pergitor|coup]] of its own in [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]],<ref name="HNN 46" /> just before the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Church [[Death/Legends|killed]] thousands of Pergitorians<ref name="HNN 46" />, exiled the [[Royal family of Pergitor|royal family]] and gained control establishing a fundamentalist theocratic dictatorship on the planet.<ref name="GG6.2" />

==Law and order==
The Church had very harsh and strict rules, and everytime a ship landed on Pergitor an [[Envoy/Legends|envoy]] was sent to its crew to read to them a list of state crimes.<ref name="GG6-1" /> Such state crimes were:
*Using any type of synthetic drug, including all forms of medication<ref name="GG6.2" />
*Exhibiting any kind of supernatural ability<ref name="GG6.2" />
*Singing, telling jokes, laughing or generally enjoying any kind of entertainment in public<ref name="GG6.2" />
*Importing any type of luxury good, including jewelry and precious metals<ref name="GG6.2" />
*Committing sacrilege of any kind against the Church of Infinite Perception<ref name="GG6.2" />

Breaking a state crime often resulted in a summary [[Death penalty/Legends|execution]], although some people had been known to get simply arrested for state crimes such as laughing in public. Citiziens of Pergitor were also required to participate in group confessions that were organized weekly.<ref name="GG6.2" />

Despite its own rules, the Church itself was one of the largest operators in the [[Black market/Legends|black market]], reguarly organizing shippings of luxury goods. 15 years after the establishment of the theocracy, this fact was still unknown to the public. <ref name="GG6.2" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Church of Infinite Perception, alongside [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Pergitor]], was first mentioned in [[West End Games]]' [[Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters|Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters]]. Despite it not giving a precise date for the events it covers, Galaxy Guides are supplements to WEG's [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]] which is set in the years after [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope]] but before [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back]]. Dating the supplement to the time period of the core rulebook would place the [[Coup on Pergitor|Church's coup]] between [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]] and [[12 BBY/Legends|12 BBY]].

On [[March 7]], [[2002]] the official ''[[Star Wars]]'' website [[HoloNet News (original website)|Holonet News]] that was created as part of the marketing campaign for the [[2002]] theatrical release of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] posted [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 46]]<ref name="HNN 46" /> featuring an article about the coup, dating the event to [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]] and subsequently preponing all of Pergitor's history by about eight years.
